args.body:
REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM
Investment Advisory Agreement — Counterparty Markup Analysis
Practice Area: Funds / Asset Management
Output: redline-review-memorandum.docx

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

This memorandum reviews the counterparty's redlined Investment Advisory Agreement against the firm standard form, internal playbook expectations for funds/asset-management engagements, the base deal materials, the disclosure schedules and exhibits, and the controlling deal-team instruction.

The counterparty accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces four material deviations:

  (1) Silent reduction of the indemnification cap;
  (2) Conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping (first-dollar) basket;
  (3) Expansion of the Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") definition with carve-outs for regulatory action of the type at issue in this matter; and
  (4) A new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations.

Disclosure schedules and exhibits further qualify the base package and must be read together with the markup: Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries), Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities), and Exhibit B (survival matrix). Scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials.

Controlling client instruction (latest partner email): the client will concede the basket conversion, but any reduction of the survival period is a walk-away issue. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority are superseded and must not be followed.

Recommended posture (subject to Section VII):
  • Basket conversion (deductible → tipping): ACCEPT / CONCEDE per client instruction.
  • Survival-period / limitation-period shortening: REJECT — walk-away.
  • Indemnification cap reduction: REJECT or COUNTER to restore firm-standard cap; escalate if pressed.
  • MAE regulatory carve-outs: REJECT or narrowly COUNTER; reconcile expressly against Schedule 3.7.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
II. SCOPE, SOURCES, AND METHODOLOGY
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A. Operative Sources Reviewed
  1. Deal materials — funds-asset-management base file (Matter File 15): engagement background, key provision framework (representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, termination), open issues, and engagement instruction to prepare this redline review memorandum.
  2. Counterparty markup — funds-asset-management: identifies the four deviations listed above and requires reconciliation against the base materials before drafting.
  3. Schedules and exhibits — funds-asset-management: Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B, each of which intersects a markup deviation; scheduled exceptions control over general base-material statements.
  4. Deal correspondence — funds-asset-management: partner email thread; only the latest message controls analysis priorities.

B. Excluded Material
  Misfiled administrative correspondence in the matter folder (unrelated engagement / distractor) was identified and is not relied upon for any recommendation in this memorandum.

C. Analytical Framework
  For each deviation we (i) state the firm-standard / base position, (ii) describe the counterparty change, (iii) reconcile against schedules/exhibits and regulatory context typical of investment-advisory arrangements (Advisers Act fiduciary and disclosure framework, client AUM / fee mechanics, and regulatory-inquiry risk), (iv) apply the controlling client instruction, and (v) assign Accept / Reject / Counter with negotiation notes and fallback language concepts.

D. Practice Vocabulary
  Funds and asset management: investment advisory agreement; advisory fee / management fee; AUM; fiduciary standard; Advisers Act; Form ADV; soft-dollar / best execution; most-favored-nation (MFN) fee concepts where implicated; Material Adverse Effect; indemnification cap, basket (deductible vs. tipping), and survival; disclosure schedules; walk-away issues.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
III. BASELINE — FIRM STANDARD FORM AND PLAYBOOK EXPECTATIONS
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Although the counterparty accepts most firm-standard provisions, the internal playbook for investment advisory agreements in this practice typically preserves the following baseline economics and risk allocations (as reflected in the base materials' key-provision framework and Exhibit B survival matrix):

  1. Indemnification Cap. A defined aggregate cap on indemnifiable losses (commonly tied to fees paid / a stated dollar ceiling / or a percentage of AUM-related consideration), with customary carve-outs from the cap for fraud, willful misconduct, and certain fundamental representations (authority, enforceability, Advisers Act registration/status, and fee calculation integrity).

  2. Basket Structure. A deductible (true deductible) basket: indemnitor pays only amounts in excess of the basket threshold. Playbook preference is deductible over tipping, because tipping recharacterizes the basket as a pure claim threshold and shifts first-dollar exposure once the threshold is crossed.

  3. MAE Definition. MAE is defined tightly, without open-ended carve-outs for regulatory investigations, examinations, or enforcement actions of the type that are foreseeable in an investment-advisory relationship—especially where the disclosure package already surfaces pending regulatory inquiries.

  4. Survival / Limitation Periods. Core and fundamental representations survive for the period set in Exhibit B's survival matrix (and related limitation-period mechanics). Playbook treats unauthorized shortening of core-rep survival as high-severity, deal-economics-altering risk.

  5. Interaction with Schedules. Disclosure schedules qualify representations; they do not silently reallocate indemnification economics or rewrite MAE. Where a schedule discloses risk (e.g., pending inquiries or retained liabilities), the agreement text should not add carve-outs or cap/basket changes that effectively leave the client uncompensated for those known items if they mature into loss.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
IV. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

────────────────────────────────────────
DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification Cap (Silent Reduction)
────────────────────────────────────────

A. Base / Standard Position
  Firm-standard indemnification cap at the negotiated baseline level, with customary carve-outs from the cap for fundamental matters and culpable conduct. Cap quantum is a principal economic term and must be transparent in the redline.

B. Counterparty Markup
  The indemnification cap is silently reduced. "Silent" reduction is particularly problematic: it obscures a material economic shift, increases the risk of missed internal approval, and undermines comparison to fee/AUM economics and any insurance tower supporting the adviser.

C. Schedule / Exhibit Reconciliation
  Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift. A reduced cap, layered on retained-liability disclosure, can leave the client with (i) known retained exposures on Schedule 5.2 and (ii) a lower ceiling on recoverable indemnifiable losses for breaches and third-party claims that the base deal allocated to the counterparty. The scheduled exceptions control over general comfort language in the base materials; they do not authorize a unilateral cap cut.

D. Risk Assessment (Funds / Asset Management Context)
  • Undercompensates client for Advisers Act–related, fee-calculation, soft-dollar/best-execution, and client-mandate breaches if losses approach or exceed the reduced cap.
  • Interacts adversely with any professional-liability / E&O insurance assumptions embedded in pricing.
  • Silent drafting invites approval and opinion-process failures.

E. Client Instruction Overlay
  The controlling instruction does not authorize concession on the cap. Only the basket conversion is conceded. Cap reduction remains fully negotiable and should be resisted.

F. Recommendation — REJECT (primary); COUNTER (fallback)
  • Primary: Restore the firm-standard cap in full; require the reduction (if any) to be shown expressly in the redline with a blackline comparison to the prior draft and internal pricing memo.
  • Fallback counter: If commercial pressure requires movement, consider a modest, transparent adjustment paired with (a) expanded cap carve-outs for fundamental reps, fraud, willful misconduct, and fee/AUM calculation breaches; (b) a separate special indemnity (uncapped or higher-capped) for Schedule 5.2 retained-liability matters that the counterparty is meant to bear; and (c) no reduction in survival (see Deviation 4).
  • Do not accept "silence" as a drafting style for economic terms.

G. Suggested Negotiation Points / Language Concepts
  • Reinstate prior cap figure and definition of "Cap" / "Indemnification Cap."
  • Clarify that nothing in Schedule 5.2 reduces the Cap or converts scheduled items into buyer-retained risk beyond their express terms.
  • Preserve exclusion from Cap for fundamental representations and intentional breaches.

────────────────────────────────────────
DEVIATION 2 — Basket Conversion (Deductible → Tipping Basket)
────────────────────────────────────────

A. Base / Standard Position
  Deductible basket: losses below the threshold are borne by the indemnified party; only excess amounts are recoverable. This is the firm-standard and playbook-preferred structure.

B. Counterparty Markup
  Basket converted from a deductible to a tipping (first-dollar once threshold met) basket. Once aggregate losses exceed the basket, the indemnifying party pays from dollar one.

C. Schedule / Exhibit Reconciliation
  Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities amplify the practical effect of basket design: a tipping basket can pull scheduled or near-threshold claim clusters into full first-dollar recovery sooner, or conversely—depending on how retained liabilities are excluded from indemnification—create mismatch between what is "retained" and what counts toward the basket. The deliverable must treat basket mechanics and Schedule 5.2 as a paired issue even though the client will concede the conversion itself.

D. Risk Assessment
  Relative to a deductible, a tipping basket is less favorable to the indemnifying party and more favorable to the indemnified party. From our client's perspective (as the party protected by the indemnity in the standard framing of this markup fight), tipping is commercially better than deductible. The economic "give" is therefore primarily a concession the other side may value in a package deal—or, if roles are inverted on particular indemnity streams, must be mapped stream-by-stream.

E. Client Instruction Overlay — CONTROLLING
  Latest partner email: the client will concede the basket conversion. Earlier messages with the opposite priority ordering are superseded. The deliverable reflects the latest instruction only.

F. Recommendation — ACCEPT / CONCEDE
  • Accept conversion from deductible to tipping basket as a client-authorized concession.
  • Document the concession expressly in the issues list and approval record so it is not later mistaken for an open point.
  • Tie the concession to preservation of walk-away positions (especially survival) and to rejection of the silent cap cut—i.e., package the give rather than stacking uncompensated gives.
  • When accepting, clean up related definitions ("Basket," "Deductible," "Tipping Basket," "indemnifiable Losses counting toward the Basket") so the tipping mechanics are unambiguous, including treatment of Schedule 5.2 items (whether they count toward the basket, are excluded from indemnification, or are covered by special indemnity).

G. Implementation Notes
  • Confirm which indemnity streams (general R&W, tax, retained liabilities, Advisers Act/compliance) the tipping basket governs.
  • Avoid accidental application of tipping mechanics to streams the playbook keeps as deductible or as true special indemnities without a basket.

────────────────────────────────────────
DEVIATION 3 — MAE Definition: Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs
────────────────────────────────────────

A. Base / Standard Position
  MAE definition without broad carve-outs for regulatory action, examination, investigation, or enforcement of the kind characteristic of investment advisers. Base materials flag conditions to closing and related risk allocation as open issues requiring analysis against firm precedent and market practice.

B. Counterparty Markup
  MAE definition adds carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter. Effect: events that would otherwise constitute or contribute to an MAE (or support a closing-condition or termination analysis) are excluded from MAE by definition.

C. Schedule / Exhibit Reconciliation — CRITICAL
  Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the markup's MAE carve-outs. Reading the markup together with Schedule 3.7:
  • The disclosure already surfaces concrete regulatory-inquiry risk.
  • The new MAE carve-outs would prevent those inquiries—and developments arising from them—from counting as (or toward) an MAE.
  • Net effect: the client is told about the inquiries in the schedule but is simultaneously stripped of MAE-based remedies, walk rights, or conditionality that the base form would preserve when regulatory risk materializes or worsens.
  Scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials; they narrow representations—they do not justify expanding MAE carve-outs that nullify the deal-protection value of knowing about Schedule 3.7 items.

D. Risk Assessment (Funds / Asset Management / Regulatory)
  • Investment advisers operate under ongoing SEC (and potentially state) examination and enforcement risk; MAE carve-outs for "regulatory action" are unusually consequential in this industry vertical.
  • Two pending inquiries on Schedule 3.7 make the carve-out non-theoretical: it is aimed at live facts.
  • Carve-outs may also interact with bring-down conditions, termination rights, and any regulatory-consent or no-action conditions to closing.
  • Market-standard MAE carve-outs (general economic conditions, markets, etc., often with disproportionate-impact qualifiers) are distinct from a targeted carve-out for the precise risk already disclosed.

E. Client Instruction Overlay
  Controlling instruction does not direct concession on MAE. MAE remains a counsel-driven reject/counter item, informed by Schedule 3.7.

F. Recommendation — REJECT (primary); NARROW COUNTER (fallback only)
  • Primary: Delete the new regulatory-action carve-outs from the MAE definition. Preserve base-form MAE so that material worsening or expansion of the Schedule 3.7 inquiries (or new related actions) can still support MAE analysis.
  • Fallback counter (only if needed to close): Extremely narrow carve-out limited to the ordinary conduct of the two specifically disclosed Schedule 3.7 inquiries as they exist on the date of the agreement, with express carve-backs (i.e., still count toward MAE) for:
      – material expansion in scope, theories, or potential remedies;
      – Wells notices, enforcement recommendations, settled orders, or litigated actions;
      – findings or allegations of fraud, willful misconduct, or Advisers Act Section 206-type violations;
      – disproportionate impact relative to similarly situated advisers; and
      – any failure to disclose additional inquiries or related facts.
  • Require that Schedule 3.7 be updated and that a special indemnity and/or closing condition address the disclosed inquiries rather than relying on MAE erasure.

G. Suggested Negotiation Points / Language Concepts
  • MAE definition: strike regulatory carve-out language inserted by counterparty.
  • Cross-reference: "For the avoidance of doubt, the matters set forth on Schedule 3.7 shall not be excluded from the definition of Material Adverse Effect solely by reason of their disclosure, and no regulatory-action carve-out shall apply to such matters or any development thereof."
  • Pair with condition-to-closing / termination hygiene so MAE is not the sole protection.

────────────────────────────────────────
DEVIATION 4 — Limitation Period / Shortened Survival for Core Representations
────────────────────────────────────────

A. Base / Standard Position
  Survival of representations and warranties—and related claim-limitation periods—as set in Exhibit B (survival matrix) and the base form. Core representations (and fundamentals) receive the survival periods specified in that matrix.

B. Counterparty Markup
  A new limitation period shortens survival for the core representations, contradicting Exhibit B.

C. Schedule / Exhibit Reconciliation — CONTROLLING TEXT CONFLICT
  Exhibit B sets the survival matrix that the markup's limitation-period change contradicts. Under the schedules-and-exhibits instruction, the scheduled/exhibit framework controls over general statements and must be reconciled in the deliverable. The markup cannot silently override Exhibit B; any change requires an express amendment to Exhibit B and client approval at walk-away severity.

D. Risk Assessment
  • Shortened survival for core reps is a direct erosion of post-closing recourse for the most important advisory-agreement truths (authority, registration/status, fee terms, conflicts/disclosure, compliance policies, AUM calculation inputs, etc.).
  • Combined with a reduced indemnification cap (Deviation 1), the client faces both less time to claim and less dollars if it claims.
  • Statute-of-limitations overlays and discovery-of-breach concepts may not fully cure an express contractual shortening.

E. Client Instruction Overlay — WALK-AWAY
  Latest partner email: the client treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. This is the controlling priority. Earlier contrary ordering in the thread is superseded.

F. Recommendation — REJECT — WALK-AWAY
  • Reject in full any new limitation period that shortens survival for core representations.
  • Require conformity to Exhibit B survival matrix without modification.
  • Do not trade survival shortening for the basket concession already authorized; survival is non-negotiable under current client instruction.
  • If counterparty insists, escalate immediately as a walk-away / deal-termination decision for the client; do not "split the difference" on core-rep survival without a new, express client mandate superseding the latest email.

G. Suggested Negotiation Points / Language Concepts
  • Delete the new limitation-period language.
  • Reaffirm: "The survival periods set forth in Exhibit B shall control. In the event of any conflict between Exhibit B and any other provision of this Agreement (including any limitation period), Exhibit B prevails."
  • Preserve fraud and fundamental-representation survival (often indefinite or statute-limited) per Exhibit B and playbook.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
V. CROSS-CUTTING RECONCILIATION MATRIX
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Deviation                         | Base / Exhibit Control              | Markup Effect                         | Schedule Intersection                         | Client Instruction        | Disposition
----------------------------------|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------------------------|---------------------------
Indemnification cap reduction     | Firm-standard cap                   | Silent lower ceiling                  | Sch. 5.2 retained liabilities shifted risk    | No concession authorized  | REJECT / COUNTER
Basket: deductible → tipping      | Deductible (playbook)               | Tipping / first-dollar after threshold| Sch. 5.2 basket-counting hygiene required     | CONCEDE (latest email)    | ACCEPT (document & package)
MAE regulatory carve-outs         | Tight MAE                           | Excludes regulatory action at issue   | Sch. 3.7 two pending inquiries intersect      | No concession authorized  | REJECT / narrow COUNTER
Shortened core-rep survival       | Exhibit B survival matrix           | New shorter limitation period         | Exhibit B contradicted; exhibit controls      | WALK-AWAY                 | REJECT — WALK-AWAY

Combined-effect warning: Accepting the cap cut and survival cut together with MAE carve-outs would leave the client with disclosed regulatory risk (Sch. 3.7), shifted retained-liability risk (Sch. 5.2), less time to sue, a lower recovery ceiling, and weaker MAE-based closing/termination protection. The authorized basket concession must not become a gateway to that stacked outcome.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VI. OTHER PROVISIONS — ACCEPTED STANDARD TERMS
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The counterparty's revision accepts most firm-standard provisions outside the four deviations above. No additional material deviations are identified in the counterparty markup materials. Standard provisions (including remaining representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, and termination mechanics not modified by the deviations) may proceed on the firm standard, subject to:

  • Conforming edits required to implement the Accept/Reject/Counter positions above;
  • Consistency pass so that definitions (MAE, Losses, Basket, Cap, Survival Period, Fundamental Representations) align across the body, Exhibit B, and Schedules 3.7 and 5.2;
  • No reliance on misfiled unrelated correspondence for any "market" or "client" position.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VII. RECOMMENDED MARK-UP POSTURE AND NEGOTIATION PACKAGE
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A. Give
  1. Basket conversion to tipping — ACCEPT per controlling client instruction. Clean drafting; clarify Schedule 5.2 counting rules.

B. Hold / Reject
  2. Survival / limitation-period shortening for core representations — REJECT; walk-away. Exhibit B controls.
  3. Silent indemnification cap reduction — REJECT; restore standard cap (or transparent, approved alternative with enhanced carve-outs and Schedule 5.2 special indemnity).
  4. MAE regulatory-action carve-outs — REJECT; protect Schedule 3.7 pathway into MAE and related deal rights. Narrow fallback only if commercially unavoidable, with strong carve-backs.

C. Packaging
  Lead with the authorized basket concession as the commercial give. Condition constructive movement on restoration of the cap, deletion of MAE regulatory carve-outs (or acceptance of the narrow fallback), and untouched Exhibit B survival. State expressly that survival is non-negotiable under current client authority.

D. Process / Approvals
  • Circulate this memorandum to the deal partner and client sponsor before returning paper.
  • Flag walk-away survival issue on the face of the issues list.
  • Require any future change to survival priorities to be in a new written client instruction that expressly supersedes the latest email.
  • Keep the misfiled unrelated correspondence out of the working set.

E. Drafting Follow-Ups Before Signature
  • Conform Exhibit B and body limitation language.
  • Update Schedules 3.7 and 5.2 as needed for accuracy at signing/closing.
  • Run a definition consistency check (MAE, Cap, Basket, Survival).
  • Confirm insurance and fee/AUM economics still support the indemnity package after any agreed cap discussion.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VIII. CONCLUSION
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Four counterparty deviations require action. One—the basket conversion—is accepted under the controlling client instruction. Three—silent indemnification cap reduction, MAE regulatory carve-outs that intersect Schedule 3.7's two pending inquiries, and shortened core-representation survival that contradicts Exhibit B—should be rejected, with survival elevated to walk-away. Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities magnify the cost of any cap concession and must be addressed expressly if economics move. Misfiled unrelated correspondence was disregarded.

This memorandum constitutes the comprehensive redline review deliverable requested for the funds/asset-management investment advisory agreement engagement (output: redline-review-memorandum.docx).

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
END OF MEMORANDUM
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
